newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Action to void contract cannot ignore jurisdiction clause.
newsitem.headline: Action to void contract cannot ignore jurisdiction clause.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that parties to commercial contracts cannot avail themselves of special jurisdiction rules to protect consumers and thereby avoid agreed jurisdiction clauses.
Where trade contracts include a jurisdiction clause, the court said these should be respected, even if one of the parties seeks to void the entire contract.

The court distinguished a jurisdiction clause, which serves a procedural purpose and is governed by the Brussels Convention on civil and commercial matters, and substantive provisions of the main contract which are governed by the court in the state in which jurisdiction rests.

"It is consonant with the aim of legal certainty that the court seized should be able readily to decide whether it has jurisdiction on the basis of the rules of the Convention, without having to consider the substance of the case", the court said.

The legal certainty jurisdiction clauses in contracts could easily be jeopardized if one party to the contract could suspend Convention rules by claiming the contract is void under substantive law, the court said.

A dispute arose under a franchising agreement between an Italian business, Dentalkit, and an Italian individual, Francesco Benincasa, operating in Germany. The contract, which had yet to be fully implemented, contained a jurisdiction clause that all disputes would be resolved in Italy.
Benincasa sought to void the entire contract under German law, basing an argument for jurisdiction in Germany under consumer rules set up under the Convention.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the Oberlandesgericht Munchen (Germany) pending between

on the interpretation of the first paragraph of article 13, the first paragraph of article 14 and the first paragraph of article 17 of Convention of 27 September 1968 on jurisdiction and the enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, as amended by the Convention of 9 October 1978 on the accession of the Kingdom of Denmark, Ireland and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (OJ 1978 L 304, p.1; amended version of the Convention at p.77)

1. The first paragraph of article 13, the first paragraph of article 14 and the first paragraph of article 17 of the Convention of 27 September 1968 on jurisdiction and the enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, as amended by the Convention of 9 October 1978 on the accession of the Kingdom of Denmark, Ireland and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, must be interpreted as meaning that a plaintiff who has concluded a contract with a view to pursuing a trade or profession, not at the prestent time but in the future, may not be reagrded as a consumer.

2. The courts of a contracting state which have been designated in a jurisdiction clause validly concluded under the first paragraph of article 17 of the Convention of 27 September 1968 also have exclusive jurisdiction where the action seeks in particular a declaration that the contact containing that clause is void.
